title: Elon Musk attacks OpenAI - here's Sam Altman's response

comments.author: @zalzalahbuttsaab
comments.text:
It is good at standard tasks such as text manipulation and interpretation. It's God awful at Arabic grammar meta-analysis, particularly root meanings and verb derivatives and struggles with visualisation tasks. It's very good at rhetoric but I don't really need it for that. For my general purposes it's great: "summarise this article in German"; "explain this for a five year old"; "give me a detailed history of chewing gum". For more insightful stuff such as conceptualising and interrogating a 3D model that is used to calibrate real world objects, it's totally pants. It's good but it can't do everything. It's the Emperor's new clothes or the man behind the curtain at the moment so is it AGI? Not a chance. But it could be.
8:54 Given that nobody knows how the first protein was formed and given the infinite complexity of the interconnectome and given that if we had all the time in the universe to randomly create a less than modest protein (which is impossible), we still wouldn't have life. It's a nice idea but in the realms of fanciful thinking.

comments.author: @nts9
comments.text: So AI is becoming a lot more powerful which means that it is becoming dangerous if it’s not controlled, Open AI must restrict AI’s capabilities to prevent people from being harmed, the problem is that if people have access to AI that isn’t controlled they will have magical powers and if they use those powers to benefit themselves and harm others we will be in extreme danger and I don’t know of anything to stop that from happening.
